text: Everything this course has built lives in someone's head unless it's written down. 'The model works' is a claim about behavior. A model card lets someone else verify that claim without re-running every eval.

This isn't invented for this course — it comes from a 2019 Google research paper, and it's become close to a de facto standard, required by Hugging Face and mapping onto the EU AI Act's documentation requirements.
Model details, intended use — what it's for and explicitly what it's not — training data, evaluation results with real numbers, ethical considerations, and caveats where it's known to fail.
Intended Use is where real-world harm gets prevented cheaply. A model tested for one task, deployed undocumented into a role it was never evaluated for, is a known pattern behind real incidents.
A model card written once and never touched again goes stale the moment the model changes. Next up: incident response — what happens when something still goes wrong anyway.
